facts.text: Sorrento earned its name when explorer John Murray, noting a resemblance to Italy’s Sorrento, renamed the area from Sullivan Bay in 1869.
In 1874 George Coppin launched the Sorrento‑Queenscliff Steam Navigation Company, sending the paddle steamer Golden Crown between Port Melbourne, Sorrento and Queenscliff.
The Continental Hotel, erected in 1875, is one of Sorrento’s many limestone‑built grand hotels that showcase the town’s distinctive stone architecture.
Built in 1877 from local limestone, the Mechanics’ Institute now houses the Nepean Historical Society’s museum and is classified by the National Trust.
Sorrento Tennis Club once occupied land beside the museum and today exists as a sunken garden, reflecting the town’s early sporting culture.
The Sorrento Sharks football team has claimed Mornington Peninsula league flags in 2004, 2008, 2010, 2011 and 2012, showcasing local sporting pride.
